summary: Backend-only (pytest + static review) testing for the comtypes.gen import-order fix in /app/awaketoggle_fix/awaketoggle/badge_win.py. All 53 pytest tests passed (0.60s), including the new regression test test_badge_win_generates_comtypes_module_before_import which mocks comtypes and asserts (a) read_badge returns 698 and (b) comtypes.client.GetModule is called exactly once with 'UIAutomationCore.dll' BEFORE any `from comtypes.gen...` import. Static review of badge_win.py confirms correct import ordering in both _automation() (line 41 GetModule precedes line 42 import) and toolbar_buttons() (line 49 _automation() call precedes lines 50-51 imports). win32.py selftest path flows through toolbar_buttons/read_badge, which now ensures the comtypes.gen submodule is generated prior to import, so the original ModuleNotFoundError('No module named comtypes.gen') cannot recur. badge.parse_number and Runner before/after badge logic (browse_runner.py) are covered by existing passing tests (e.g. 'Zähler 698 → 698' assertion).
critical_code_review_comments: badge_win.py is clean; import order is now correct in both _automation() and toolbar_buttons(). No further changes needed.
Minor nit: _ocr() uses subprocess.run without checking stdout emptiness distinctly from errors; already handled defensively by parse_number returning None.
Consider caching toolbar_buttons result briefly to avoid repeated UIA tree walks when read_badge is called before+after each browse (optional perf; not a bug).

rca of the issue: RCA: `from comtypes.gen.UIAutomationClient import ...` requires the comtypes.gen submodule to exist, which is dynamically generated only after comtypes.client.GetModule('UIAutomationCore.dll') runs. The original code in toolbar_buttons() imported from comtypes.gen BEFORE calling _automation() (which runs GetModule), causing ModuleNotFoundError on first use. Fix: call _automation() first (line 49), then do the `from comtypes.gen...` import (lines 50-51). Same pattern inside _automation() itself (GetModule on line 41 before import on line 42). Verified by mocked unit test that asserts GetModule is invoked exactly once prior to the gen import and read_badge returns the badge value 698.
